newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Ramos says trade gap must be narrowed.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Ramos says trade gap must be narrowed.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Thursday the Philippines would have to narrow its trade deficit to sustain financial stability.
In a speech at the Central Bank's fourth anniversary celebrations, Ramos said "our external payments position is far from totally secure."
"The trade deficit, which represents some 13 percent of gross national product, must be brought down."
"We must ever be alert against untoward pressure on our currency," he said, even if the current account deficit was at a manageable level of 4.1 percent of GNP in 1996.
Ramos' warning comes in the wake of a speculative attack on the peso after Thailand's de facto devaluation of the baht on Wednesday.

Though the trade and current account deficits were being offset by steady flows from overseas workers' remittances, the fickleness of capital flows, particulary portfolio investments, have been worrisome, he said.
